newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - Copper focus on Third Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - Copper focus on Third Wednesday.

text.p: The copper market may be poised for more volatility this week as July tightness starts coming to a head during Monday's Third Wednesday pricing, analysts and dealers said.
Although the tightness had been well signed, prices might spring higher as dates became prompt, they said.

"There has been some good borrowing in the nearby dates and it's all very tight until you get into August. If those tighten up further, you could see prices come up a little bit," said analyst Helen Williamson of brokers Brandeis.
Tightness was concentrated from Wednesday, the July date, to the end of the month. On Friday, July/one day was at a backwardation of $13, July for one week was at $47 and July/threes at $122.
London Metal Exchange chief executive David King told Reuters on Friday that the exchange was keeping an eye on copper, saying it and zinc were "sensitive" at the moment.
The long side of the market was believed by some traders to be a major merchant or investment interests who were squeezing Far Eastern shorts.
The market was even buzzing with the possibilty of the daily backwardation reaching the LME's limit of one percent -- currently around $25.
Technically, an upside break initially targeted $2,300 per tonne, chartists said. Prices were probing that level during Monday's pre-market after finishing Friday $16 firmer at $2,284.
A confirmed breach of the level would then target a vast chart gap between $2,308 and $2,365, created when copper tumbled more than $100 overnight last Wednesday in a bout of fund liquidation.
But there was no guarantee that copper could sustain an upside move as technical charts and market sentiment remained muddled, analysts said.
"At the same time it is still vulnerable to go lower. It depends on what the funds are going to do, so people are very confused about what it's going to do next," Williamson said.
With attention glued to nearby tightness, the market had ignored a week-long strike at Portugal's Neves Corvo 107,000-tonne per year copper mine.
Miners over the weekend approved a temporary deal to return to work on Monday, and management was due to present a new proposal for the operation of continuous working by Wednesday.
Among the other metals, Third Wednesday might elicit a reaction in aluminium if a heavy pricing requirement emerged.
Prices popped higher on Friday towards the key $1,600 level despite what traders called an unsurprising 6,900-tonne LME stock increase.
Many traders said it reflected off-warrant consignment metal being registered. LME stock data showed 10,000 tonnes landed in Rotterdam.
Zinc, having consolidated somewhat after its latest upward spurt, was open to further gains, with $1,500 as the next big target.
